description: Attempted to toggle nanoex off (from true, confirmed matching the app) while Kevin had the official app open checking current Cooling/NanoeX state (view only, confirmed no changes made in-app). Rejected -- new error code, apparent 2-minute lockout of unclear origin (see corrected notes).

error.message: 他の機器でエアコンが制御されました。2分間変更できません。
error.message_en_approx: The air conditioner was controlled by another device. Cannot be changed for 2 minutes.

notes: Third distinct E-21291-* code seen this session (after 00002 clock-skew, and 00007/01712 generic-application-error family). This one has a specific, actionable message rather than a generic apology.

RE-CONFIRMED theory (at the time): it IS a cross-client write conflict. Kevin reports the official app fires a real PUT ('writing settings' modal) just from opening and closing the NanoeX menu, even with zero value change -- so even though he never changed anything, the app itself still wrote. That write (from the app, a different client) is almost certainly what put the appliance into the 2-minute lockout that then rejected our CLI's write. The earlier 'self-cooldown from our own prior write' correction was wrong -- reverting to the original cross-client-lockout theory, now confirmed rather than guessed.

FURTHER CONTEXT, 2026-09-23 later (during real HA integration testing): the same lockout was reproduced through HA's own writes ALONE, back-to-back ~18s apart, with Kevin explicitly confirming no other app/client was connected at THAT time. Kevin then clarified that during THIS earlier CLI session, a separate Eolia app instance actually was running on an AVD (Android emulator) the whole time -- not mentioned until later -- so the cross-client explanation above likely genuinely applies to this specific capture. But since the same lockout also happened with confirmed zero other clients (see 37), a real second client isn't NECESSARY to trigger it -- 'another device' in the error message doesn't reliably describe the actual mechanism in every case. Current leading theory: a write-timing-based cooldown (hardware/compressor protection, or operation_token continuity) that any two writes close together in time can trigger, whether or not they're really from different clients. See exceptions.py's EoliaDeviceLockedError docstring and capture 37 for the fuller picture.

Real implication for the HA integration: writes can transiently fail with this ~2-minute lockout for reasons not fully understood -- possibly just from HA's own write cadence, not only external app/remote use. Mapped this code to a distinct exception (EoliaDeviceLockedError) with an actionable message rather than a generic HomeAssistantError. Worth testing later whether echoing the last operation_token back on the next write avoids triggering this.
Did NOT retry immediately -- waiting out the ~2 minute window before re-attempting the nanoex toggle, to avoid hammering the endpoint during an active lockout.
